note: Our synthesis of public sources, reviewed by hand. Rankings are judgement, not official lists.

Norway.title: Mass drone and missile attacks
Norway.why: Norway has almost no defence against cheap drones and ballistic missiles. The most likely attack is a drone-and-missile campaign on energy, ports and bases, not a ground invasion.
Norway.startup: Cheap, layered counter-drone for the Home Guard and critical sites.

Norway.title: Sabotage at sea and on the seabed
Norway.why: Subsea cables, pipelines and offshore energy feed Europe. PST reports Russian and Chinese mapping of coastal infrastructure.
Norway.startup: Underwater sensing, seabed monitoring and anomaly detection.

Norway.title: Too few people for a huge territory
Norway.why: A long coast and Arctic border with a small population and a small army. Adding people is not realistic.
Norway.startup: Autonomy and remote operation, so one operator runs many systems.

Norway.title: Too slow from idea to capability
Norway.why: Most big programmes mature in 2029–2036, but the threat window is 2027–2029. Speakers at the Oslo DefSec Forum said Norway has the money but buys too slowly.
Norway.startup: Ship fast, prove it in tests, and use open purchasing systems to get in early.

Norway.title: Weak domestic production and supply security
Norway.why: In a crisis the shop is closed. Powder, explosives, spare parts and components are bottlenecks, and too little of the Ukraine money is spent in Norway.
Norway.startup: Additive manufacturing, local production and components free of Chinese parts.

Europe.title: Air and missile defence, drones included
Europe.why: The EU names air and missile defence its first capability gap. Only a third of EU counter-drone programmes are expected to deliver by 2030.
Europe.startup: Interceptors and sensors that are cheaper than the threat.

Europe.title: Not enough ammunition, missiles and factories
Europe.why: Europe cannot yet produce at wartime volume. Ammunition and missiles are a named EU priority, and Ukraine shows how fast stocks run out.
Europe.startup: Manufacturing tech, automation and suppliers to the primes.

Europe.title: Russia's hybrid campaign
Europe.why: Arson, sabotage, cyberattacks, GPS jamming and drone incursions against countries that back Ukraine, below the threshold of war.
Europe.startup: Critical-infrastructure protection, cyber and resilient navigation.

Europe.title: Slow and fragmented procurement
Europe.why: 27 national markets and slow processes. The Commission's own draft says the 2030 readiness goals are at risk despite record spending.
Europe.startup: Sell to several countries at once through joint buys and EU programmes.

Europe.title: Dependence on the US for key enablers
Europe.why: Satellites, ISR, airlift and communications still depend heavily on the US, and Washington is reviewing its troop deployments.
Europe.startup: European space ISR, secure comms and data, free of US export control.

Norway.title: Counter-drone: cheap detection and interceptors
Norway.why: Detection is the bottleneck. Passive radar, acoustic and RF sensors plus interceptor drones, built for the Home Guard.

Norway.title: Uncrewed systems in the air, on the surface and under water
Norway.why: Forsvaret runs an open NOK 600 m purchasing system for drones, and the Navy is getting unmanned systems for infrastructure protection.
Norway.examples: Six Robotics, Maritime Robotics, Kongsberg HUGIN

Norway.title: Underwater sensing and seabed protection
Norway.why: Norway leads in autonomous underwater vehicles and hydroacoustics, and has the most seabed infrastructure to guard.

Norway.title: EW-resilient comms and navigation without GPS
Norway.why: Russia jams GPS in the north. Systems must keep working when links and satellites are denied.

Norway.title: AI for command, control and sensor fusion
Norway.why: C2 at operational level is one of Norway's worst bottlenecks; the new C2 suite is not ready before 2030. Forskningsrådet funds a more data-driven defence.

Europe.title: Drones and counter-drones at scale
Europe.why: The European Drone Defence Initiative is one of four EU flagships. Drone and interceptor makers are raising the biggest rounds.

Europe.title: Low-cost interceptors for air defence
Europe.why: Shooting down a cheap drone with an expensive missile does not scale. NATO DIANA lists scalable air-defence countermeasures as a challenge.
Europe.examples: Cambridge Aerospace, Ukrainian interceptor makers such as Vyriy

Europe.title: AI and autonomy for uncrewed systems
Europe.why: Multidomain autonomy is a DIANA challenge area, and AI-first companies are Europe's most valuable defence startups.

Europe.title: Space-based ISR and secure communications
Europe.why: Europe wants its own eyes and links in orbit to reduce dependence on the US.

Europe.title: Electronic warfare, cyber and resilience in contested environments
Europe.why: AI, quantum, cyber and EW form one EU priority area, and operational resilience is a DIANA challenge.
Europe.examples: Ukrainian EW makers, Nordic cyber firms
